chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ishaq ibn Ghalib, from Abu Abdillah عليه السلام.
In a sermon of his, specifically mentioning therein the state of the Prophet and the Imams عليهم السلام and their qualities.

So our Lord, by reason of His forbearance, deliberateness, and compassion, was not prevented by the enormity of their crimes and the ugliness of their deeds from choosing for them the most beloved of His Prophets to Him, and the most honored of them before Him, Muhammad ibn Abdillah عليه السلام. His birth was in the very midst of honor, and his lineage-root in the depth of nobility; his ancestry was unblemished, his lineage unmixed, and his description was not unknown to the people of knowledge. The Prophets gave glad tidings of him in their books, the scholars spoke of him in their descriptions, and the wise pondered him through his attributes. Refined, unmatched; Hashimite, without equal; of al-Abtah, unsurpassed. His trait was modesty, and his nature generosity; formed upon the dignities and morals of prophethood, stamped upon the qualities and forbearances of messengership, until the causes of the decrees of Allah reached in him their appointed times, and by the command of Allah the decree proceeded concerning him to its final ends; the inevitable decree of Allah brought him to its utmost goals.

Every community gave glad tidings of him to the one after it, and every father passed him on to a father, from loins to loins. No illicit union mixed his substance, and no unlawful relation defiled him in his birth, from Adam to his father Abdillah, within the best lineage-group, the noblest stock, the strongest clan, the most protected womb, and the safest lap.

Allah chose him, approved him, and selected him, and gave him the keys of knowledge and the springs of wisdom. He sent him as a mercy to the servants and a springtime for the lands, and Allah sent down to him the Book, in which are clear expression and full clarification.
“An Arabic Qur'an, without any crookedness, so that they may attain taqwa.”

He has made it clear for the people, laid out its path with knowledge, detailed it, clarified a religion, obligated duties, defined limits for the people and explained them, and disclosed matters to His creation and proclaimed them. In it are indications toward salvation and landmarks that call toward His guidance.

So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله conveyed what he was sent with, proclaimed openly what he was commanded with, fulfilled what he had been burdened with from the weights of prophethood, showed patience for his Lord, strove in His way, sincerely advised his community, called them to salvation, urged them to dhikr, and guided them to the path of guidance by means of ways and calls whose foundations he established for the servants, and by beacons whose signs he raised for them, so that they might not go astray after him; and he was toward them compassionate and merciful.

key_terms.أَوْقَارِ النُّبُوَّةِ: The dignified qualities and gravities of prophethood
key_terms.اِنْتَجَبَ: He selected and chose with special preference
key_terms.حِلْمِهِ: His forbearance and restraint in dealing with creation
key_terms.مَحْتِدُهُ: His ancestral root and noble family origin
key_terms.مَفَاتِيحَهُ: Its keys, meaning the openings and access points of knowledge
key_terms.مَقَادِيرِ اللَّهِ: The divine determinations and decreed measures of Allah
key_terms.مَنَارٍ: Beacons or landmarks set up to indicate guidance

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the lineage, character, and mission of the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This sermon describes the noble lineage, pre-eternal recognition, exalted character, and divinely decreed mission of the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله. It presents him as Allah’s chosen mercy, bearer of the clarifying Qur'an, and the one who fully conveyed the message, guided the الأمة, and established enduring signs of guidance.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Is’haq Bin Ghalib, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
in a sermon of his<sup>asws</sup> especially mentioning therein the state of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> and the Imams<sup>asws</sup> and their<sup>asws</sup> description: -

‘So our<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> was not prevented, due to His<sup>azwj</sup> Forbearance and His<sup>azwj</sup> Care, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Kindness, from the greatness of their crimes and the ugliness of their deeds, that He<sup>azwj</sup> should Choose for them the most Beloved of His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophets to Him<sup>azwj</sup>. 
And He<sup>azwj</sup> Honoured them upon it, Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> Bin Abdullah<sup>saww</sup> with regards to the respectability of his<sup>saww</sup> linage, and regarding the prestigious-ness of his<sup>saww</sup> family environment, without there being a blemish in his<sup>saww</sup> descent nor an inter-mingling in his<sup>asws</sup> lineage, nor being unknown in the presence of knowledgeable people of his<sup>saww</sup> description which the Prophets<sup>as</sup> had given glad tidings with, in their<sup>as</sup> Books, and the scholars had spoken with his<sup>saww</sup> epithet, and the wise ones had pondered on his<sup>saww</sup> description. 
A mannerism which no Hashimite had reached or was an equivalent of, nor had a person of Bat’ha had ever reached to such a peak. And his<sup>saww</sup> nature was generous and had a natural tendency upon the dignity of the Prophet-hood and its mannerisms, bring naturally upon the qualities of the Messenger-ship and its magnanimity, up to that he<sup>saww</sup> ended up to the Pre-determinations of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> to its timings, and there flowed, by the Command of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the Ordainments with regards to him<sup>saww</sup> up to its end goals, fulfilling the Inevitable Ordainment of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> to its peak.

Every community gave the glad tidings of it from after him<sup>saww</sup>, and every father handed it over to a father, from back to back.  There did not did not mix it in the cutthroat race and did not defile the marriage in his<sup>saww</sup> linage from since Adam<sup>as</sup> up to his<sup>saww</sup> father<sup>as</sup> Abdullah<sup>as</sup>, being in the best of the parties, and the most prestigious of tribes, and the most protected of groups, and the most preserved of lap, and the safest of laps.

Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Chose him<sup>saww</sup>, and Favoured him<sup>saww</sup>, and Selected him<sup>saww</sup>, and Gave him<sup>saww</sup> from the Knowledge, its keys, and from the Wisdom, its springs, a Mercy to the servants, and a Sustainer to the cities. An Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed the Book unto him<sup>saww</sup> wherein were the statements and the explanations,
[39:28] An Arabic Quran without any crookedness, that they may fear.

He<sup>azwj</sup> had Explained it to the people and Programmed it with knowledge. He<sup>azwj</sup> had Detailed it, a Religion He<sup>azwj</sup> had Clarified it, and necessities He<sup>azwj</sup> had Obligated these, and Legal Punishments He<sup>azwj</sup> had Defined these for the people and explained these, and matters he<sup>saww</sup> has uncovered to His<sup>azwj</sup> creatures, and Proclaimed therein the evidence to the salvation and information Calling to His<sup>azwj</sup> Guidance.

So Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> delivered what He<sup>azwj</sup> had been Sent with, and expounded openly with whatever he<sup>saww</sup> had been Commanded with, and fulfilled whatever he<sup>saww</sup> was carrying from the burden of the Prophet-hood, and observed patience for his<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, and struggled in His<sup>azwj</sup> Way, and advised to his<sup>saww</sup> community and called them to the salvation, and urged them upon the Remembrance (Zikr), and pointed them upon the way of the Guidance by manifestos and prepared grounds of foundations for the servants, and raised beacons for them as their signs, perhaps they might not stray from after him<sup>saww</sup>, and he<sup>saww</sup> was kind and merciful with them’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from father from al-Hassan ibn Sayf from his father from those he mentioned from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
“Once the Holy Prophet (s.a) addressed the people and he raised his right hand while holding his fingers closed and said, ‘Do you know, O people, what is in my hand?”
They said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.”
He then said, “In my hand there are the names of the people of Paradise, the names of their fathers and the names of their tribes up to the Day of Judgment.
He then raised his left and asked, ‘O people, do you know what is my hand?”
They said, “Allah and His Messenger know best.”
He then said, “In my hand there are the names of the people of Hell, the names of their fathers and the names of teir tribes up to the day of Judgment.”
Then he said, “Allah has decreed and He has done justice. Allah has decreed and He has done justice. One group will go to Paradise and the other group to Hell.”
